text: CrazySexyCool is the second studio album by American girl group TLC, released on November 15, 1994, by LaFace and Arista Records. Following their debut album Ooooooohhh... On the TLC Tip, released in 1992 to positive reviews and commercial success, the group began working on a follow-up in 1993 but faced an unproductive recording process due to personal issues, particularly those involving member Lisa "Left Eye" Lopes, who was struggling with alcoholism and her volatile relationship with football player Andre Rison. The album's recording spanned from late 1993 to September 1994, during which Lopes' involvement diminished as she was in rehab after pleading guilty to an arson incident in which she set fire to Rison's tennis shoes in their shared mansion, claiming it was an accident stemming from abuse and frustration; she was sentenced to five years probation and therapy at a halfway house. The group reunited with producers Dallas Austin, Kenneth "Babyface" Edmonds, and Jermaine Dupri, as well as new collaborators Organized Noize and Chucky Thompson, with Sean "Puffy" Combs contributing to the hip hop soul sound. The album features hip hop beats, funk, deep grooves, propulsive rhythms, and smooth production, marking a lyrical departure from their debut, exploring themes of sexuality, romanticism, inexperience, and youthful optimism. It was critically acclaimed and commercially successful, peaking at number three on the Billboard 200 and staying on the chart for over two years. Certified 12-times platinum by the RIAA on October 11, 2019, it has sold over 23 million copies worldwide and is the best-selling album by an American girl group. It has been included in Rolling Stone's list of The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time, the book 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die, and was listed as a "New Classic" by Entertainment Weekly in 2008. It was ranked number seven on Billboard's list of the best diamond-certified albums of all time. The album's production took place at studios including Doppler Studios, Bosstown Recording Studios, KrossWire Studio, GADaddy's, D.A.R.P. Studios in Atlanta, the Music Grinder Studios in Los Angeles, and The Hit Factory in New York City. The group worked with producers including Babyface, Dallas Austin, Jermaine Dupri, and Organized Noize, with Phife Dawg from A Tribe Called Quest providing interludes. During recording, members were not always in the studio together due to scheduling conflicts. "Waterfalls," written by Lopes, Marqueze Etheridge, and Organized Noize, features vocals from all three members, with background vocals by Debra Killings and Cee-Lo Green, whom Tionne Watkins called a longtime friend from Goodie Mob. The song references 1990s issues such as violence linked to drug trade and the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with Watkins noting the importance of conveying the message without preaching. The album was seen as a rebellious, non-conventional departure from traditional R&B, blending sensual R&B with edgy hip-hop spirit. Compared to their debut, which was described as "kiddie-cute hip-hop," CrazySexyCool featured adult-female sexuality and "hide- and-seek coyness," viewed as a coming-of-age project with themes of youthful optimism and inexperience. All four singles reached the top five on the Billboard Hot 100, with two reaching number one: "Creep" topped the chart for four weeks and was ranked number three in Billboard's Year-End Hot 100 Singles of 1995; "Red Light Special" peaked at number two; "Waterfalls" spent seven weeks at number one and was the second-biggest single of 1995; "Diggin' on You" reached number five. The album debuted at number 15 on the Billboard 200, selling 77,500 copies in its first week, and peaked at number three with 117,000 units sold by July 1995. It was nominated for six Grammy Awards in 1996, with "Waterfalls" nominated for Record of the Year and Dallas Austin and Babyface nominated for songwriting; TLC won Best R&B Album and Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals for "Creep." The group also won multiple awards at the Billboard Music Awards, American Music Awards, Soul Train Music Awards, and MTV Video Music Awards, including four awards for the "Waterfalls" video, including Video of the Year and Viewer's Choice. The album was recognized as a landmark in R&B, influencing modern artists through its fusion of hip-hop and R&B, and was celebrated in a 2021 concert tour marking 27 years since its release, which included 18 U.S. dates and honored it as the album that truly put TLC on the map. As of July 2006, the album had sold over 23 million copies worldwide, and as of July 2017, it had sold 7.7 million copies in the United States, becoming the best-selling album by a female group in the country. Internationally, it reached number one in New Zealand and the top five in Australia, Germany, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom.
